articleTitle: Optimal Charging Scheduling of Electric vehicles for Smart Grid Operations Employing Demand Side Management strategy with Battery Storage System
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment (ICEPE)
abstract: This study dives into the critical area of smart grid optimization, with an emphasis on cost minimization through the integration of demand side management (DSM) and electric vehicle (EV) dynamics. The development of renewable energy sources, as well as the increasing use of electric vehicles, have created challenging situations for traditional grid management. Using sophisticated optimization techniques, this paper presents a complete framework to improve the efficiency and economic feasibility of smart grid operations. By carefully integrating DSM tactics with EV charging patterns, the suggested model aims to reduce peak demand stresses, reduce grid congestion, and optimize energy distribution. To accomplish these objectives, a load scheduling-based DSM has been applied in this work. With the application of DSM using Frilled Lizard Optimization (FLO) has achieved 3.7% of cost reduction and 33.46% reduction in peak load when Battery was not considered. When battery is considered, there is 0.7% reduction in cost whereas the peak load has been reduced significantly by up to 48.18 %. The suggested optimization technique for DSM application has produced superior results in fewer iterations.

articleTitle: Automatic Weather Station
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment (ICEPE)
abstract: A weather station can be described as an instrument or device which provides information of the weather in its neighboring environment. For example, it can provide readings of temperature, humidity, pressure, wind speed, light intensity etc. The system consists of power supply, a set of sensors, microcontroller to receive input data from sensors, processes them and provides information through display system. A low-cost weather monitoring system has been designed. The power supply to the system is provided by converting AC mains to desired DC voltage. Also, an option has been kept to get power supply from battery. The battery is charged using solar panel. This will help in getting uninterrupted power supply. Various types of weather parameters like temperature, humidity, pressure, wind speed, rain, light intensity will be measured by using different sensors. The data collected by these sensors will be sent to the microcontroller. The microcontroller analyses the input data and gives output signal as text to be displayed in mobile. The weather monitoring system is portable in size having reliable data which will be highly useful for various sectors like aviation, agriculture, shipping, road transport, power and energy, disaster management, defense, tourism, pilgrimage, mountaineering, fishing, urban development, sports, health etc.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Cost-Effective PV String I-V and P-V curve tracer by using IGBT as a Power Electronic Load
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment (ICEPE)
abstract: The I-V curve tracer serves as a vital instrument for capturing the I-V characteristics of photovoltaic (PV) strings, reflecting variable environmental conditions. This device finds widespread application in assessing power generation performance and detecting potential faults within PV strings. To ensure heightened accuracy and rapid data acquisition, numerous I-V tracer techniques have been developed and proposed. This paper introduces a novel and cost-effective approach for tracing string-level (1500V DC, 20A) I-V and P-V curves, leveraging an IGBT as a variable load. The gate voltage of the IGBT is precisely controlled by a PWM signal from a microcontroller. A comparative analysis is conducted under standard temperature and illumination conditions, comparing the manufacturer's datasheet with simulations using MATLAB/Simulink. Additionally, a comparison is made between the manufacturer's datasheet and experimental data to evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed technique. The methodology presented in this study aims to provide an efficient and economical solution for tracing I-V and P-V curves at string level, contributing to the accurate assessment of PV string performance and fault detection.

articleTitle: Smart Battery Charge Monitoring with Auto-Detection of Individual Battery and Accountability
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment (ICEPE)
abstract: Electric vehicles are used around the world because it has benefits of protection against the environment and its resources. The present system is about finding the battery's parameters and its performances based on cloud data storage for the purpose of battery analysis. Our project is emphasizing on detecting a battery automatically when connected to the charging unit with the help of RFID technology. To maintain auto accountability of history of charging time and frequency of charging, it is focusing on the concept of smart charging based on IoT. IoT in the EV charging system is responsible for connecting the EV owners with the information of the battery. The acquired information can be used to analyze the battery's performance and compare charging times and statuses with previous records. Auto detection mechanism will provide services such as automatically detecting the battery and storing data without any conflicts, thus preventing accidental battery exchanges. Also, the number of Electric Vehicles is increasing and so is additional demand of power system. To address this issue, EV Smart Charging Stations are much needed.

articleTitle: Enhancing Demand Response Forecasting Through Random Forest Regression: A Case Study Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment (ICEPE)
abstract: Demand response (DR) plays a crucial role in optimizing energy consumption and ensuring grid reliability. This study investigates the efficacy of Random Forest Regression (RFR) as a predictive tool for DR forecasting, focusing on its performance within the context of a specific dataset. Utilizing data on residential energy consumption patterns, we conducted a comparative analysis of RFR against alternative regression algorithms. The results reveal promising outcomes, suggesting that RFR outperforms other models in terms of predictive accuracy and generalizability, particularly within our dataset. Furthermore, the study explores parameter optimization strategies and assesses the impact of varying 'n_estimators' on model performance. The findings underscore the potential of RFR in forecasting load dynamics, thereby facilitating informed decision-making in DR program planning and implementation. This research contributes valuable insights into enhancing DR forecasting methodologies, paving the way for more effective and sustainable energy management practices.

articleTitle: Analytical Study on Multi Layered Micro-level MEMS Energy Harvester with or without Seismic Mass for Low Power Remote IoT Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment (ICEPE)
abstract: High efficiency in piezoelectric energy harvesting is critical for numerous reasons. For instance, the power generated by piezoelectric devices is often low, hence maximizing conversion efficiency is critical to ensure adequate energy production for practical applications. The existence of proof mass has a significant impact on the efficiency and performance of piezoelectric energy harvesters. This study compares two cantilever beam configurations—one without a proof mass and the other with proof mass, in order to investigate the effects of proof mass on the performance of piezoelectric energy harvesters. The cantilever beam with a proof mass produced much greater output voltage, peaking at 26.1 V, using COMSOL Multiphysics simulations. The improvement is achieved by the proof mass raising the oscillation amplitude and resonance frequency of the beam, which increases mechanical strain and electrical output. This study emphasizes the significance of proof mass in improving the energy conversion efficiency of piezoelectric energy harvesters.

articleTitle: Enhanced parameter optimization of PID controller for single area power system using hybrid ALO-GBO algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment (ICEPE)
abstract: This paper focuses on applying two evolutionary algorithms, Ant Lion Optimization (ALO) and Gradient-based Optimization (GBO), to enhance load frequency control (LFC) in a power system. LFC is crucial for stable power operation, but traditional methods struggle with system complexity and uncertainties. ALO mimics lion hunting behavior, while GBO uses gradients for optimization. Both are known for tackling complex problems. The study implements these algorithms in a single-area power system model, tuning controller parameters to minimize frequency deviations and improving the performance. This paper includes mathematical modeling, algorithm implementation, and result analysis to show how hybrid of both ALO and GBO algorithm improve stability and performance as compared to traditional methods.

Author Keywords: LFC-Load Frequency control-Automatic Generation Control.ISE-Integral Square Error

articleTitle: Noise Reduction Technique in ECG Signal
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment (ICEPE)
abstract: An electrocardiogram (ECG) signal is a biomedical signal which records the electrical signal from the heart of the human body. The ECG signals are merged together with different kinds of noise signals, such as baseline wander, powerline interference, high-frequency noises, etc., which will create obstacles for any physician and lead to improper treatment of patients. This article proposes the design of different filters to remove or reduce such noises from the ECG signal so that accurate information can be traced for the treatment of patients.

articleTitle: Bidirectional power flow of BLDC drive-based pump hydro storage connected to a grid-tied PV network
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment (ICEPE)
abstract: Pump hydro energy storage (PHES) is vital for grid stability. The traditional system lacks flexibility, so variable-speed machines are gaining attention. The study focuses on a variable-speed brushless direct current (BLDC) machine in PHES applications with a grid-tied solar photovoltaic framework. A single-phase grid side converter and a BLDC drive employ a d-q controller to achieve bidirectional power flow. Maximum power point tracking and a rule-based algorithm are used for optimal operation and energy management, respectively. The proposed topology offers benefits such as IEEE 519-compliant total harmonic distortion, DC bus voltage, and BLDC speed control. Results from MATLAB/Simulink show potential for reliable and sustainable energy architecture development.

articleTitle: A non-singular terminal sliding mode controls base voltage and frequency control in an islanded microgrid
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment (ICEPE)
abstract: The microgrid parameters such as frequency and voltage are deviating from the standard value due to external disturbance. In island microgrids, maintaining parameter values near the standard value is mandatory to ensure a reliable supply of electricity to consumers. Therefore, this paper adopts an efficient and reliable control technique called Non-Singular Terminal Sliding Mode Control (NS-TSMC). The NS-TSMC is resilient against several uncertain loads and disturbances. NS-TSMC has the property to converge in finite time. The suggested control strategy is executed in MATLAB/Simulink environment, and the productiveness was examined under dissimilar load values and uncertainties. The results are compared with the existing PI anti-windup control approach. The fine voltage and current regulation of the NS-TSMC controller ensures the islanded microgrid remains stable in the face of uncertainties and disruptions, demonstrating superior performance.

articleTitle: EU-Net: Efficient U-shaped Deep Convolutional Neural Network for Colon Polyps Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment (ICEPE)
abstract: Deep learning has emerged as a transformative approach in the realm of polyp segmentation within colonoscopy images. In the pursuit of advancing this segmentation approach, this study introduces a novel deep learning architecture that synergistically combines the concept of EfficientNet-B7 and U-Net and propose a new architecture named EU-Net. The EfficientNet-B7, recognized for its scalable and powerful feature extraction capabilities, serves as the encoder of EU-Net. In contrast, the U-Net, renowned for its capability in biomedical image segmentation, functions as the decoder. The prime contribution of the proposed model lies in the analysis of different attention mechanisms before the concatenation of skip connection and the upsampling feature. This attention mechanism enhances the model’s focus, ensuring it retains critical regions within images, thereby boosting the accuracy of segmentation tasks. Furthermore, the EU-Net model is enriched with dilated convolutions, enabling it to capture multi-scale context without the loss of resolution, a paramount feature for detecting polyps of varying sizes. The proposed model was rigorously evaluated using the CVC-ClinicDB, a benchmark database for colonoscopy image analysis. The proposed model achieves an IoU of 0.8863. Preliminary results showcase a substantial improvement in segmentation performance, highlighting the potential of the proposed Eu-Net in advancing colorectal cancer prevention efforts.

articleTitle: AI and ML in Finance: Revolutionizing the Future of Banking and Investments
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment (ICEPE)
abstract: The advent of a new age in banking and investments is being heralded by the fast development of AI and ML technologies within the sector. This essay delves into the potential of AI and ML to revolutionize the future of finance by boosting productivity, precision, and decision-making skills while reducing exposure to risk. Financial organizations may increase their development and profit by leaps and bounds by using this cutting-edge technology. The identification and prevention of fraud is a crucial use case for AI and ML in the financial sector. To detect fraudulent actions, machine learning algorithms may examine massive data sets, looking for trends and outliers. Financial institutions may protect their customers' funds and maintain their patrons' faith by taking this preventative measure. Chatbots and virtual assistants driven by AI have completely altered the banking industry's approach to customer support. Intelligent bots like this use NLP and sentiment analysis to tailor their responses to each unique consumer and suggest items that would best meet their financial requirements. This improves happiness among paying customers and simplifies business operations, which saves money on labor. Another industry that AI and ML have revolutionized is investment management.

articleTitle: Advanced Security System for four wheeler: Minimizing Collision Accidents through Collision Avoidance Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment (ICEPE)
abstract: This project aims to develop an advanced and cost-effective solution to enhance safety in various environments by preventing collisions between objects. Employing Arduino microcontrollers and a range of sensors, the system operates in real-time to identify obstacles and take immediate corrective actions. Key components include ultrasonic sensors for accurate distance measurement, an Arduino microcontroller for data processing, and actuators such as motors or servos for executing avoidance maneuvers. By analyzing sensor data, the Arduino assesses obstacle proximity and triggers suitable responses to avoid collisions. The project introduces a flexible and scalable framework suitable for integration into different applications, including robotics, autonomous vehicles, and smart environments. Moreover, emphasis is placed on user-friendly customization, allowing end-users to adjust system parameters and behaviors according to specific requirements. Addressing the growing need for safety solutions in autonomous systems, robotics, and IoT applications, the Collision Avoidance System represents a significant advancement in reliable collision avoidance technologies. By providing an accessible and adaptable platform, the project facilitates the development of technologies that can reduce accidents, enhance operational efficiency, and promote the widespread adoption of autonomous systems across various domains.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Energy Efficient Single Phase MLI based Autoclave System With Proper Coil Parameter Selection
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment (ICEPE)
abstract: In this work, a hybrid switched capacitor multilevel inverter (SCMLI) based induction heating (IH) system, which combines multilevel inverter (MLI) and autoclave load is proposed to enhance the performance of the system for IH applications. The primary disadvantage of MLI is it requires numerous switches and dc sources. As a result, the size, cost, and complexity of MLI rises, and its efficiency declines. To overcome this issue SCMLI is considered to fed the autoclave load. In comparison to conventional MLI the proposed topology utilizes less number of components with boosting capability. Moreover this topology offers lower harmonic distortion and higher efficiency. To provide the gate signals to the switches phase disposition pulse width modulation technique (PDPWM) is adopted. Also the mathematical modelling of the litz wire based coil is performed to calculate the accurate resistance and inductance of the coil. To validate the performance of hybrid system, MATLAB simulation and laboratory results are provided.

articleTitle: An Online Signature Identification System Utilizing ReliefF Feature Selection Technique and Multi Class Optimizable SVM Classifier
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment (ICEPE)
abstract: Automatic signature identification is a trending research area and has importance. So, this research presents an online signature identification method that utilizes "ReliefF" feature selection algorithm and an optimizable multi-class SVM classifier. The objective of our work is to identify a person to give him/her access to a confidential area/system. Feature selection is a critical area. So, to choose the most suitable features describing a particular class is critical. Therefore, we used the "ReliefF" feature selection algorithm to minimize classification error and remove the least relevant features. Moreover, Signature verification still is a challenging research problem because of large intra-class variations and small interclass variations while considering forgeries. Therefore skilled forgery signatures of each user are used here as a separate class to enhance the identification accuracy of the proposed system resulting into multi-class classification problem. Use of K fold cross validation has enhanced the efficiency of machine learning model on unseen data. We used an optimizable multi-class SVM classifier with a Bayesian optimizer to tune the hyper parameters. The use of "ReliefF" selected features has enhanced testing accuracy of the model. The proposed system is trained, validated and tested on the SVC2004 Database (Task 1) for five and all forty users having different types of signature information yielding promising identification results.

articleTitle: Performance and Economic Evaluation of wind-based Microgrid solution for Pakke Kessang, Arunachal Pradesh
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment (ICEPE)
abstract: The study assesses PAKKE KESSANG's potential for wind energy generation through statistical analysis of wind data using the Weibull distribution. It suggests establishing microgrids using local clean energy sources to enhance power generation resilience. Microgrid deployment is deemed beneficial for integrating renewable energy sources efficiently. The research evaluates the technological and economic feasibility of wind-powered microgrid systems with energy storage. Four microgrid scenarios are compared using metrics like Net Present Cost and Levelized Cost of Energy, with wind-based microgrids showing lower Net Present Cost (NPC) but higher Levelized Cost of Electricity (LCOE) than grid-connected counterparts. HOMER Pro Microgrid software is used for analysis.

articleTitle: Hyperspectral Band Selection using Modified Jaya Optimization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment (ICEPE)
abstract: Hyperspectral (HSI) data provide vast amount of data which contain spatial and spectral information about each pixel of an image, which is useful in detecting objects and identifying materials. However, the information provided by the HSI image is challenging to process. Hence, compression of HSI makes it easier to utilize the data without the need for any heavy computation.The proposed methodology aims to modify Jaya Algorithm by fine-tuning the number of cluster heads, to select the bands which are rich in information. The proposed model was implemented on the datasets, Pavia University and Indian Pines. The band selection results were evaluated by comparing with Multi-Verse Optimizer(MVO) and Particle Swarm Optimization(PSO). The experimental findings demonstrate the superior efficacy of the proposed model in comparison to several extant models.

articleTitle: Investigating THD for Series Arc Fault Detection in Single-phase Electrical Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment (ICEPE)
abstract: Series arc fault (SAF) detection is a laborious challenge when the electrical network includes multiple electrical installations. Moreover, arcing deteriorates the quality and life of the utilities that are connected to the network. This is because arcing can inject strong harmonics into the circuit which is greater than the widely accepted range. In this work, the feasibility of SAF detection using the total harmonic distortion (THD) in current for individual & combined electrical, and electronic loads is explored. From the analysis, it is inferred that this investigation aids in identifying the limit for THD eventually leading to reliable series arc fault detection.

Author Keywords: sampled rate of rise in current

articleTitle: Plant Disease Detection using Feature Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment (ICEPE)
abstract: Plant diseases are one of the biggest threats in today’s world, it impacts yield of crop in a big way. Early detection is vital for effective disease management, prompting the need for advanced methodologies. This work addresses the challenge of plant disease detection through an innovative approach using spectral data and image data. The focus is on improving accuracy and efficiency in identifying diseases at their early stages. Our motivation to improve upon existing work stems from the limitations of standalone techniques that exist currently, emphasizing the potential of spectral data and image data. By performing the detection models of diseases in plants, with the help of spectral data and image data, we aim to increase the accuracy of the models with the help of ensemble learning, and feature fusion.

articleTitle: Validation of Electric Field Intensity in Non-thermal Plasma Reactor Using COMSOL Multiphysics
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment (ICEPE)
abstract: This study explores the multifaceted aspects of non-thermal plasma (NTP) generation through the simulations using COMSOL Multi-physics. Validation of the electric field intensity of various electrode types, carrier gases, and reactor materials have been done using these simulations. All the possible combinations of considered variations have been simulated and found the maximum and minimum electric field distributions inside the reactor for each case. It has been found that the maximum electric field intensity is not varying much with respect to variation in ground electrode material and carrier gas type, while there is a significant variation with respect to reactor material. Quartz glass tube is found to be best suitable for the present application, as it shows strong electric field intensity, i.e. 1.81 MV/m, compared to that of borosilicate with all other parameters constant. This study helps in deciding the operating parameters for NTP treatment of diesel exhaust to reduce NO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">X</inf> concentrations.

articleTitle: Shunt Active Filter for Harmonic Compensation at Electric Vehicle Charging Station based on p-q Theory
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment (ICEPE)
abstract: In recent times, to reduce the dependency on fossil fuels there is a significant increase in electric vehicle usage. Many EV charging stations are being established and connected to the power transmission grid. During the charging process, harmonics are introduced in the grid by the high power chargers which are present in the charging station and can cause power quality issues. In this paper, a model of equivalent charger and electric vehicle charging facility is established to analyse the supply current harmonics. Then the compensating devices such as passive and active harmonic filters are utilised to eliminate the harmonics in order to enhance the power quality of the grid.The mathematical model for the configuration of filters is also presented . The Matlab/Simulink platform is used for the simulation of EV charging station, which includes high power chargers and harmonic compensators.The simulation results of supply current are compared before and after the introduction of passive and active harmonic filters.The results shows that after the compensation by filter equipments the current harmonics are within the specified limits.

articleTitle: Machine Learning based Brain Tumor Detection and Classification System
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment (ICEPE)
abstract: The field of automated anomaly detection in medical imaging has become a fast developing subject, particularly in various medical diagnostic applications. In the context of Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI), the automated detection of tumors holds significant importance, offering crucial insights into abnormal tissues essential for treatment planning. The conventional way of detecting defect in MRI brain images was human inspection, but its practicality diminished over time due to larger datasets. To address this challenge, automated tumor detection methods have been developed, aiming to save radiologists’ time. However, the complexity and variability of tumors make the process of MRI brain tumor detection inherently intricate. In this paper, tumor is detected and classified in brain MRI images using machine learning algorithms. The proposed work illustrates that CNN model shows highest accuracy and can be considered as a superior analyzing tool for detecting and classifying brain tumors.

articleTitle: Hyperspectral Unmixing for Highly Correlated Endmembers using Scaled Endmembers and Abundance Sparsity Constraint NMF
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment (ICEPE)
abstract: Hyperspectral unmixing (HU) is an essential process in remote sensing that involves decomposing hyperspectral images into distinct spectral signatures (endmembers) and their corresponding fractional abundances. However, handling highly correlated data in HU can be difficult, as traditional methods often perform inadequately. This paper introduces a novel method for hyperspectral unmixing called Scaled Endmembers and Abundance Sparsity Constraint Non-negative Matrix Factorization (SEA-NMF). The method incorporates a scaling mechanism for endmembers to enhance distinctness among the endmembers. Additionally, we include an abundance sparsity constraint to account for the spatial distribution of the hyperspectral image, which in real scenarios has a minimal number of endmembers that contribute to each pixel. Experiments on both synthetic and real hyperspectral datasets have demonstrated that SEA-NMF outperformed existing unmixing techniques in terms of reconstruction error and endmember estimation accuracy, when highly correlated endmembers are involved. The results demonstrate that our method successfully addresses the challenges caused by highly correlated data, offering a robust tool for better hyperspectral image analysis.

articleTitle: Development of a High-Gain DC-DC Converter for Hydrogen Fuel Cell Based Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment (ICEPE)
abstract: Electric vehicles (EVs) powered by hydrogen fuel cells utilize a high-gain DC-DC converter to boost the fuel cell's low voltage output to the higher levels required by the electric motor and battery storage systems. Ensuring a consistent and reliable power supply is crucial for optimizing the performance and range of a car during operation. This paper introduces an innovative high-gain converter designed specifically for electric vehicles powered by fuel cells. It utilizes a unique combination of a quadratic boost converter (QBC) and a hybrid voltage doubler circuit. The design prioritizes achieving outstanding efficiency and reducing switching stress, which is essential for maximizing the performance and lifespan of fuel cell-driven electric vehicles. By conducting a thorough analysis and experimentation, we aim to confirm the effectiveness of this hybrid converter for efficiently transforming fuel cell output to meet the power requirements of modern electric vehicles. The results highlight the promising prospects of this integrated approach in enhancing the sustainability and performance of electric vehicle technology.

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis and Evaluating Active Suspension System Controllers with CoppeliaSim
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment (ICEPE)
abstract: This comparative analysis examines the efficacy of popular active suspension system (AS) controllers, including PID, LQR, and fuzzy logic controllers, in terms of stabilization time(s<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">t</inf>) and maximum car body displacement(CBD). While LQR demonstrated the fastest (s<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">t</inf>, fuzzy logic and PID controllers emerge superior due to their ability to minimize maximum CBD, which is crucial for handling and comfort. The PID controller achieved a minor displacement of 0.08m, with fuzzy logic close behind at 0.15m. Research directions include a datadriven approach to tuning the rules in fuzzy logic using direct input-output data from the quarter car model to surpass the performance of expert-driven fuzzy logic rules. Finally, the fractional-order PID controller with its integrator order (µ) and derivative order (λ) parameters has the potential to outdo the performance of conventional PID controllers. This paper shows that dynamic simulation software like CoppeliaSim is essential in system visualization and analysis for system design and optimization to achieve optimal vehicle dynamics and ride comfort.

articleTitle: Detection Of Diabetic Retinopathy Using Deep Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment (ICEPE)
abstract: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) remains a critical concern in the realm of ophthalmology, demanding accurate and efficient diagnostic methodologies. This paper presents a comprehensive approach leveraging deep learning algorithms for the detection of DR. Our methodology integrates several stages of processing to enhance the accuracy and robustness of the detection system. Firstly, we employ autoencoders to resize and normalize the datasets, ensuring uniformity and optimal input for subsequent processing stages. Additionally, a denoising convolutional neural network (CNN) is utilized to mitigate noise within the data, thereby enhancing the reliability of subsequent analyses. Furthermore, preprocessing techniques including Contrast Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization (CLAHE) are applied using MATLAB, augmenting the quality and contrast of retinal images for improved feature extraction. Subsequently, a CNN based on InceptionV3 architecture is employed for segmentation, feature extraction, and classification. This CNN framework enables effective identification of pathological features indicative of DR, facilitating accurate diagnosis. The proposed methodology demonstrates promising results, achieving high accuracy, up to 95.6 percent in detecting diabetic retinopathy from retinal images. Through the integration of advanced deep learning techniques, our approach offers a reliable and efficient solution for early diagnosis and intervention in diabetic retinopathy cases.

articleTitle: Exactly Discretized Model of FitzHugh Nagumo Oscillator Using Taylor-Lie Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment (ICEPE)
abstract: This paper proposes an exactly discretized model for FitzHugh-Nagumo oscillatory system. A recent technique of discretization, Taylor-Lie discretization is used for the exact discretized model. Exact discretization for nonlinear models is new and the proposed model has been compared with canonical discretization technique to establish the quality of Taylor-Lie discretization approach. A set of system theoretic analyses supports the obtained results which includes time response analysis, phase portrait analysis, effects of sampling time T and external stimulus I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ext</inf> on the system state trajectories have been presented and discussed. The efficiency of the proposed approach have been explored on the basis of approximation error visible in simulation results.

articleTitle: Highway Hypnosis Detection and Prevention System
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment (ICEPE)
abstract: Highway hypnosis is a phenomenon where a driver can become inattentive and experience a decrease in awareness while driving on long, monotonous stretches of road. In this paper, we propose a Highway Hypnosis Detection and Prevention System (HHDPS) using computer vision techniques. The goal of the system is to identify highway hypnosis symptoms in real time and alert the driver in order to prevent possible accidents. In this work, we present the system model, the model used for detection (Dlib library), and experimental results, and conclude with insights on its effectiveness.

articleTitle: Behavioral Analysis of Stock Using Selective Indicators from Fundamental Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment (ICEPE)
abstract: In the current digital era of free trading and changing work culture, markets worldwide gained momentum for retail investors to trade from anywhere with ease. According to Bloomberg, the number of retail traders rose to 24% of the market from 15% pre-pandemic [1]. Most of them are young retail traders with high-risk tolerance compared to the previous generation of retail traders. As a result of that, there are many market predictors, and market data sellers are on the rise. These companies are charging investors a subscription fee. Young traders are inclined to subscribe to these predictors assuming one of them is right. According to financial reports on Wall Street, 90% of retail traders are on the losing end. In this paper, we are studying multiple indicators and trying to derive behavioral patterns from the underlying stock.There are two major categories of indicators that traders and investors would like to follow, Technical and fundamental respectively. Famous investor like Warren Buffet follow a methodology called "Value investing" which is based on fundamental analysis. In our paper, we chose multiple indicators from fundamental analysis to understand the behavioral patterns of stocks based on those indicators [2]. For the purpose of research, we have picked Apple stocks from 2015 to 2019. We believe after COVID, the market moved significantly, both positively and negatively. Since it’s an external factor that influenced the pricing, we have decided not to include that data in our study. To study the behavioral pattern of price action for the stock over 5 years, a total of 8 indicators are chosen from fundamental indicators such as Debt to Equity Ratio (D/E), Book Value Per Share, Price to Earnings Ratio (P/E), Price to Book Value (P/B), Volume, Price to Sales, Price to Free Cash Flow, Dividend Yield.

articleTitle: Unsupervised Land Use Land Cover Mapping of Sentinel-2 Data using Convolutional Autoencoders
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment (ICEPE)
abstract: The increasing importance of Multispectral image analysis in recent years is particularly evident in the domain for monitoring land use land cover. This is crucial for addressing complex issues such as food production loss, heightened vulnerability to disasters, and the broader impact on climate. One significant challenge in this realm is the proper management of land use, which necessitates accurate and up-to-date land use land cover maps. Our work employs an unsupervised approach to generate land use land cover maps using Sentinel-2 Multispectral datasets of 2018. A Convolutional Autoencoder extracts high-level features from season-wise stacked data, followed by the Hierarchical Clustering Algorithm to systematically organize and classify land use patterns. This unsupervised technique demonstrates the effectiveness of hierarchical clustering in creating detailed and informative land use land cover maps over time. This highlights the application of unsupervised learning in generating meaningful insights from land use land cover maps, showcasing its potential for enhanced analysis and interpretation.

articleTitle: Series Balancing Capacitor (SBC) based DMPPT Scheme for string of PV Modules operating under non-uniform operating conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment (ICEPE)
abstract: In a Photovoltaic (PV) system, modules are connected in series and parallel combinations to achieve desired voltage and current ratings. However, a string of PV modules can have a vastly reduced energy output during non-uniform operating conditions. This paper introduces a new Distributed MPPT (DMPPT) architecture using a Balancing Capacitor connected in series with a string of PV modules, having MPP and non-MPP functionality (where the system will output a desired amount of power). Each PV module in this scheme has a partial power processing (PPP) DC-DC converter connected across them to allow them to operate at a desired voltage depending on the system requirements. In comparison to other DMPPT schemes, this architecture can easily be integrated with a DC grid without the need of additional power electronic stages, at the same time allowing the PV modules to operate at their maximum power points (MPPs) if the system demands it. This scheme has been validated using detailed simulations and results are presented to verify the proposed architecture.

articleTitle: Power Quality Improvement in Distribution Network using DSTATCOM
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment (ICEPE)
abstract: The development of power electronic devices in modern applications has caused a decline in power quality in distribution networks due to an increase in nonlinear loads on the consumer side. Problems include harmonic currents, imbalanced loads, inadequate voltage regulation, and high reactive power demand are symptoms of this deterioration. The distortion of the supply current caused by harmonic currents makes them a major concern. To address this problem, this paper utilizes a Distribution Static Synchronous Compensator (DSTATCOM) setup employing Sinusoidal Pulse Width Modulation (SPWM) and a Synchronous Reference Frame (SRF) extraction approach. MATLAB/Simulink is employed to model and simulate the DSTATCOM system. The PWM generator is calibrated using the DQ theory as a fundamental principle to power the DSTATCOM. A thorough evaluation of the DSTATCOM’s performance enhancements is carried out by a comprehensive analysis of total harmonic distortion (THD). This method improves power quality and reduces harmonic currents in the distribution network.

articleTitle: Extended Kalman Filter Based Estimation of the State of Charge of Lithium Iron Phosphate Battery Using an Equivalent Circuit Model
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment (ICEPE)
abstract: State of charge (SoC) estimation is vital for battery management systems in electric vehicles (EVs). Lithium-iron phosphate (LFP) batteries, known for their power density, cycle life, and thermal stability, present unique challenges due to flat voltage and hysteresis effects. This study employs a pulse current test to identify parameters for two RC Equivalent Circuit Models (ECMs) and uses the Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) for SoC estimation. Three ECMs are developed and compared, with the model incorporating a hysteresis correction factor (HCF) showing superior performance. Validated with Dynamic Stress Test (DST) and Federal Urban Driving Schedule (FUDS) cycles, the HCF model reduces average error and RMSE significantly, demonstrating robust and accurate SoC estimation for LFP batteries

articleTitle: Reconfiguration based Even-Odd Column Shifting to Achieve Maximum Power Output in Shaded PhotoVoltaic System
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment (ICEPE)
abstract: Solar power plants increased more attraction and the demand for electrical energy in next few years is benchmarked. When PV arrays are exposed to Partial shading it leads to irregular row current and show the local Maximum power Point in P-V characteristics. In this paper, an Even-Odd column shifting based array reconfiguration model is suggested. The array reconfiguration method is proposed that rearranges the position of the modules based on the column in 9×9 Total Cross Tied configuration within an array to improve the maximum power under shading. The different parameters viz. losses are evaluated based on four shading patterns. The Even-Odd column method is compared with Total Cross Tied (TCT) and Dominance Square (DS) to show the best performance. The advantage of the Even-Odd column reconfiguration is the positions are rearranged within the column itself, so the wiring requirements is easy.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Arduino based low cost Autonomous Car
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment (ICEPE)
abstract: In today's era of technological innovation, the quest for autonomous vehicles has become a captivating endeavor. Our venture introduces an ingenious solution: an Arduino-powered autonomous car, meticulously designed to navigate its surroundings independently, promising an immersive journey into the realm of robotics. At the heart of our creation lies a symphony of components: motor controllers infusing life into the wheels, ultrasonic sensors acting as vigilant sentinels against obstacles, and a mastermind microcontroller, Arduino, orchestrating every maneuver with precision. The working model is more than just assembling parts; it's a learning adventure. Aspiring engineers get practical experience with electronics, programming, and robotics. They learn how to combine sensors, map routes, and control devices in real-time. Looking beyond the horizon, our vision extends to further innovation. Imagine integrating advanced sensors for heightened environmental awareness, deploying cutting-edge algorithms for seamless localization and mapping, and establishing wireless connectivity for remote oversight and command. In essence, our Arduino-based autonomous car isn't just an endeavor; it's a testament to ingenuity, a gateway to exploration, and an invitation to redefine the boundaries of possibility in the realm of autonomous robotics.

articleTitle: A Novel Control of 2DOF PID based Grid Connected PV – Wind Hybrid Sytem
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment (ICEPE)
abstract: Nowadays, hybrid renewable energy based grid integrated systems are extensively utilized. These systems commonly integrate PMSG coupled wind power generation and Photovoltaic systems due to their advantages. However, the power generation from wind relies on wind velocity, while Photovoltaic power generation relies on solar irradiance. Consequently, power production from both sources can be inconsistent. To tackle this issue, an efficient control method must be implemented to inject the generated power into the utility grid. The study compares the effectiveness of the 2DOF PID controller with Proportional & Integral and Mamdani Fuzzy controllers in managing abrupt system changes. The control strategy proposed, utilizing 2DOF PID controllers, is tailored for the DC and AC sides of the grid-connected system. Its objective is to link the wind-PV hybrid system with the grid seamlessly. This sophisticated control method not only compensates for the reactive power demanded by loads, but also reduces the harmonics produced by nonlinear loads, and maintains balanced grid currents even when unbalanced loads are linked to the PCC. Hence, the proposed control methodology can be able to improve the power quality by supplying quality power at local bus. Additionally, the control strategies implemented in the DC-DC converters for wind and PV systems allow for optimal operation at the maximum power point across different scenarios. Extensive results are gathered from hardware-in-the-loop experiments using OPAL-RT devices.

articleTitle: Speed Control of DC Motor Driven Electric Vehicle Model Using Dynamic Surface Control
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment (ICEPE)
abstract: In this paper, speed control of DC motor driven Electric Vehicle (EV) using dynamic surface control is proposed. The dynamic surface control design requires a first order low-pass filter to avoid unlike derivative terms, cause ‘explosion of terms’, present in the other available robust and optimal control techniques such as PID control, sliding mode control and backstepping control etc. Required asymptotic stability condition is derived via Lyapunov Stability theory, and the closed-loop EV system's performance is assessed. Finally, the MATLAB simulation is performed to demonstrate how well the designed dynamic surface control can control the and stabilize speed of DC driven EV model.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Microstrip Patch Antenna with Defected Ground Structures for Biotelemetry Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment (ICEPE)
abstract: Limitations in Microstrip Patch Antennas (MPA) have led to an increasing amount of research in the development of these antennas, especially for biotelemetry applications. This paper focusses on enhancing the performance of a rectangular MPA for biotelemetry devices through the incorporation of defected ground structures (DGS) of different shapes. The proposed antenna resonates at the Industrial, Scientific, and Medical (ISM) band of 2.45GHz frequency. Three different shapes of DGS; U-slot, circular-slot and L-slot are analyzed wherein the number of these slots are increased from one to four along the four corners of the ground plane. With a patch dimension of 32.04mmx40.56mmx0.05mm the antenna is compact and it is designed, optimized, and simulated in CST microwave studio. The performance of all the designed antennas are compared and it is found that the antenna with two L-slot DGS gives optimized result with a return loss of -48.78dB, a bandwidth of 0.031GHz, and a stable gain of 6.40dBi which is 52.80% higher compared to the conventional MPA without DGS.

articleTitle: Optimization of a Stand-Alone Hybrid Renewable Energy System
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment (ICEPE)
abstract: The uptake of renewable energy, the expansion of the energy markets, and business tactics all affect sustainable generation. For a hybrid microgrid system to be both economical and dependable, the right combination of different renewable energy sources and storage devices is essential. In this paper, off-grid hybrid energy systems (HES) in remote areas are examined from both a techno-economic and sustainable perspective. As the Ant Lion Optimizer algorithm (ALO) has advantages over other methods for lowering the Levelized Cost of Energy (LCOE) and Net Present Cost (NPC), it is utilized as an optimization-seeking algorithm. Furthermore, a sensitivity analysis has been conducted on every model, and the Hybrid Optimization Model for Electric Renewable (HOMER Pro) is used to conduct simulations to examine the system components.

articleTitle: Design and Development of Compact High-Voltage Source Required for Non-Thermal Plasma Jet Generation
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment (ICEPE)
abstract: This paper details the design and development of a compact high-voltage (HV) source required for the operation of non-thermal plasma jet systems. The demand for compact, reliable, and energy-efficient high-voltage sources in plasma technology has intensified recently. In response to this need, our study focuses on designing and fabricating a novel high-voltage source, considering key factors such as size reduction, energy efficiency, and reliability. The proposed compact high-voltage source is engineered to power plasma jet systems, a crucial element in various applications, including materials processing, surface treatment, and biomedical research. The report outlines the design methodology, fabrication process, and simulation results, demonstrating the successful development of the compact high-voltage source required for the plasma jet system. It was found that the unit can produce 18 kV pulse output voltage from 12 V DC input at 9 kHz frequency. The findings highlight the potential for advancing plasma technology by implementing compact high-voltage sources, paving the way for enhanced portability and versatility in diverse industrial and scientific applications.

articleTitle: Optimized Speed Regulation of Induction Motors through PI Controller Tuning with Cuckoo Search Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment (ICEPE)
abstract: This paper explores the application of optimization techniques in enhancing speed regulation in induction motor drives, particularly focusing on Direct Torque Control (DTC) systems. It specifically investigates the use of cuckoo search algorithm (CSA) for optimizing proportional-integral (PI) controllers in regulating the speed of induction motors. By utilizing CSA, optimal values for the controller’s proportional (kp) and integral (ki) gains are determined based on minimizing the Integral Square Error (ISE) of speed error. The effectiveness and adaptability of CSA in speed control are evaluated through MATLAB simulations conducted on a 0.75 kW induction motor under both load and no-load conditions. The results include waveform analyses of speed, current, and torque, demonstrating the efficacy of the CSA-optimized PI controller for achieving precise speed regulation in induction motor systems.

articleTitle: Analysis of Harmonic Generated by Household Electronic Equipments with SMPS Using Matlab® Simulink®
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment (ICEPE)
abstract: Power quality issues are on the rise due to the growing prevalence of electronic equipment, resulting in distortion of voltages and currents. When a large number of low-power, single-phase non-linear loads are present, it can lead to significant harmonic issues. This can result in elevated harmonic voltages and currents, which can be detrimental to the overall power quality of electrical systems. In this work, the household electronic devices with the switch mode power supply (SMPS) are modelled using Matlab® Simulink® to analyze their non-linear behavior. The harmonic analysis is conducted for three different household equipments with SMPS (i.e., a compact fluorescent lamp of 11 W, a light-emitting diode of 3.5W, and a personal computer of 50W) in the time-domain. Moreover, the total harmonic distortion (THD) of current and voltage of these nonlinear household loads is also discussed in this work.

articleTitle: Tuning of a Robotic Arm using PID Controller for Robotics and Automation Industry
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment (ICEPE)
abstract: This paper discusses integrating robotics and automation systems to improve industrial automation’s efficiency, precision, and reliability, focusing on the versatile robotic arm. The study explores Auto PID tuning for controlling robotic arms through MATLAB Simulink for dynamic performance optimization. The paper systematically examines PID implementation and tuning PID techniques and compares them to other controllers. In this way, it provides invaluable insights into automation control technologies. The research focuses on designing and auto-tuning a PID controller in real-time for efficient robotic arm control.The PID controller is the best option for robotic arm operation as it allows dynamic parameter modification and precise trajectory tracking. Finally, the study stresses the PID controller’s efficiency and effect in improving industrial robotic arms’ performance. It thus enables smooth operation and increases productivity in the manufacturing environment.

articleTitle: Optimizing Wind Farm Layouts for Maximum Efficiency using PSO considering wake effect
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment (ICEPE)
abstract: Wind energy is crucial for renewable power generation and optimizing turbine placement in wind farms maximizes efficiency. This study uses Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm in Python to find optimal turbine positions. Considering variable wind speeds and directions, PSO improves power output and efficiency. The research shows PSO’s effectiveness in complex optimization for wind farm layouts. The proposed layout has practical implications for renewable energy, aiding in more sustainable and efficient wind farms. Such layouts advance renewable technologies. This study highlights PSO’s potential in renewable energy optimization, stressing layout importance in effective wind energy utilization. It contributes to renewable energy planning.

articleTitle: Underwater Pipeline Detection using Deep Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment (ICEPE)
abstract: With the increasing demand for underwater infrastructure, the need for efficient and reliable methods for detecting and monitoring underwater pipelines has become paramount. This study gives a complete assessment of YOLOv8, an object detection model, in connection with detecting underwater pipelines, which can be utilized for transfer learning and future research. A comparison with prior versions, YOLOv5 and YOLOv7, high-lighting the importance of computational speed in a range of scenarios. The study examines the YOLOv8 framework and analyzes image preprocessing methods for improving detection accuracy under a variety of situations, including low light, noise, and background. Furthermore, hyperparameter tuning experiments are carried out to improve model performance by altering batch sizes, epochs, learning rates, and augmentation methods. Mean Average Precision is used to evaluate the model (mAP), which is a commonly used measure to assess how well the model can detect objects. The research evaluates the models’ resilience and generalization capabilities using mAP scores generated across a variety of test situations, highlighting the importance of YOLOv8 in infrastructure maintenance, environmental monitoring, and disaster response.

articleTitle: Design and Performance Analysis of Single Sided Magnetic Coupler for Leakage Magnetic Field Reduction in a Wireless Power Transfer System with Ferrite and Alnico material
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment (ICEPE)
abstract: Wireless Power Transfer (WPT) systems have gained popularity due to their safety and convenience in various applications. WPT enables energy transfer through magnetic fields, eliminating the need for direct electrical connections between the transmitter (TX) and receiver (RX) sides. In this study, we designed and analyzed four types of coils with different couplers using ANSYS Maxwell simulation to investigate their performance in WPT systems. The four coil designs included Type I - a circular copper coil without a coupler. Type II -a copper coil with a conventional ferrite coupler; Type III -a copper coil with an optimized ferrite coupler; and Type IV - a copper coil with an optimized ferrite and alnico coupler. Simulation results revealed that Type II, with the conventional ferrite coupler, significantly improved the coupling coefficient (k) and mutual inductance (M) compared to the coil-only design (Type I). However, this improvement also increased magnetic field density (B), raising concerns about human safety and potential electromagnetic interference (EMI) issues. To address these concerns, we proposed an optimized ferrite coupler (Type III), which maintained high coupling efficiency and mutual inductance while limiting the magnetic field density to the same level as the conventional ferrite coupler. Furthermore, we explored a hybrid coupler design (Type IV) combining an optimized ferrite and an alnico coupler, resulting in higher magnetic field density and being suitable for applications requiring more vital magnetic fields. The study emphasizes the importance of carefully optimizing coupler designs to achieve efficient power transfer while considering safety and EMI implications. These findings provide valuable insights for designing WPT systems tailored to specific application needs. In conclusion, this research contributes to the advancement of WPT technology and provides a valuable guide for optimizing coupler designs to maximize power transfer efficiency and magnetic field characteristics in WPT systems..

articleTitle: Online Signature Verification Using Chi-Square (χ2) Feature Selection and SVM Classifier
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment (ICEPE)
abstract: Signature verification is a potential research area because of its social, legal and cultural acceptance since time immemorial. Hence unlike other biometrics it is more prone to forgery. So we have proposed an online signature verification system with user specific Chi-Square (χ2) feature selection to enhance the accuracy of our system. The aim of our work is to verify the signature of a person by comparing with the reference template for the claimed signature stored in the system during enrolment. Features extraction and feature selection are critical area because many number of features may be derived for verification purpose. So, to choose the most appropriate features describing a particular class is critical because it has a high effect on accuracy of the system. Therefore, we used the χ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> feature selection algorithms to minimize verification error, decrease computational time, decrease model size and achieve higher performance. Signature verification is a very difficult work because of large intra-class variations and small interclass variations while taking into account skilled forgeries. Here the verification is done using skilled forged signatures of each users to enhance the verification accuracy. Efficiency of the model on unseen data is enhanced using k fold cross validation. In the proposed system we have used Multiple SVM with all the kernel functions to find the best performing SVM with the different numbers of Chi-Square (χ2) selected features to find out the model with most promising verification results. The Model is used on the SVC2004 Database (Task 1) yielding very good result. Accuracy achieved in our case is 92.75 %.

articleTitle: Feature estimation and parameter tuning using H∞ Filter on FastSLAM framework
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment (ICEPE)
abstract: Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) plays a key role in enabling mobile robots to autonomously navigate and build a map of their environment. Despite its wide range of applications, localization and mapping has its own disadvantages which include computation, feature representation,sensor noise, data association and robustness in dynamic environments. EKF-SLAM and FastSLAM are two frameworks of SLAM. However, they face problems related incorrect priori knowledge of mean, correlation and covariances of process as well as measurement noise as Kalman Filter acts as a minimum covariance estimator. In this paper an Extended H-infinity based FastSLAM is proposed which takes into consideration worst case minimization error and priori knowledge of noise is not essential. The proposed framework is an integration of Rao-Blackwellization Particle filter for proposal distribution and robot pose estimation along with Extended H-Infinity Filter for feature/landmark estimation. Further, the impact of the tuning parameter θ on accuracy is tested. The proposed algorithm is evaluated on a simulated environment and is compared with the existing frameworks.

articleTitle: The Energy-Efficient and Distortion Blocking Leaky Integrate-and-Fire Neuron Model
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment (ICEPE)
abstract: Neuromorphic technologies have the potential to revolutionize cognitive computing by accelerating biologically inspired learning algorithms. These algorithms and architectures rely on basic processing and memory units called neurons and synapses. In neuromorphic circuit design, there is a continuous quest to create energy-efficient and distortion-free spiking neurons for integration into neuromorphic system architectures. In this context, this paper introduces a novel approach to prevent the distortion encountered in the membrane voltage of the LIF neuron circuit. By implementing a low-power Schmitt trigger-based spike generator in the LIF neuron design, the circuit effectively mitigates distortions in the membrane voltage. The presenting leaky integrate-and-fire neuron has been realized by 12 transistors and two capacitors, which offer a significant energy efficiency advancement in contrast to their current equivalents. In addition, the LIF neuron proposal showcases optimal energy and power savings, like 8.56fJ energy consumption per spike, and the model consumes an average power of 1.62nW. Furthermore, it offers the flexibility to adjust firing frequency within the biological frequency range of 1Hz-84KHz using a control voltage V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">C</inf>. These findings highlight the potential of creating energy-efficient and distortion-free neuromorphic systems.

articleTitle: Analysis and Assessment of Green Hydrogen Development for the Future of Oman
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment (ICEPE)
abstract: Green hydrogen is a significant step toward a sustainable and carbon free future. As the world faces the challenges of climate change and the pressing need to decarbonize various sectors, green hydrogen has emerged as a promising solution. Green hydrogen, which is produced from water using renewable energy sources, is a clean, carbon-free gas that can be used to generate electricity, heat, and transport. With global demand predicted to increase from 70 million tons in 2019 to 120 million tons by 2024, hydrogen development should satisfy the United Nations' seventh objective of affordable and clean energy. Countries such as Australia, the European Union, India, Canada, China, Russia, the United States, South Korea, South Africa, Japan, and North Africa are exploring the production process using renewable energy sources. This review explores the development and potential of green hydrogen in Oman. It discusses the country’s strategic plans, the proposed methodology for green hydrogen production, the results, and discussions from recent studies, and concludes with the potential impact and prospects.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Multiple Wavelets for Robust Half-Iris Verification with SVM
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment (ICEPE)
abstract: Our experiments demonstrate that fusing features extracted from multiple wavelets leads to improved verification accuracy for segmented half-iris templates compared to single-feature methods. Support Vector Machines (SVMs) were employed for classification.We evaluated the performance of nineteen different wavelets across various decomposition levels of the Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT). When we consider only one wavelet feature, the coiflet4 wavelet at the second-level horizontal decomposition achieved the highest accuracy of 92%. Conversely, the biorthogonal 1.3 wavelet at the fourth-level horizontal decomposition yielded the lowest accuracy at 65%. These findings highlight the importance of selecting appropriate wavelets for optimal performance.When we combined multiple features, the verification accuracy increases upto of 98% for CASIA and UBIRIS databases. Hence, SVM classification with combined wavelet features proves effective for iris-based person verification.

articleTitle: F-Type Inverter fed PMSM Motor with Elliptical Reference Vector-Based Fast SVPWM Technique for EV Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment (ICEPE)
abstract: The difficulty with conventional pulse width modulation (PWM) techniques for three-level F-Type inverters (3L-FTI) is the capacitor voltage variation. The modulation scheme must be created considering all aspects of the investigated wide-speed-torque range traction drives. In the traditional field-oriented control (FOC) method, an elliptical reference vector-based multilevel space vector PWM (SVPWM) technique is introduced in this paper. Simple arithmetic operations and logical judgments are sufficient for this technique; trigonometric operations and lookup tables are avoided. Neutral point (NP) voltage balancing is achieved with fewer switching intervals during start-up using a modified virtual SVPWM method(VSVPWM). Experimental results from a 3L-FTI prototype with different speed-torque scenarios and simulation results from a Simulink model are employed to demonstrate the efficacy of the suggested algorithm.

articleTitle: Micro-Hydro and Solar Synergy: A Review of Hybrid Power Solutions for Assam’s Energy Challenges
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment (ICEPE)
abstract: Assam, a region grappling with escalating electricity demands and pressing environmental concerns, the reliance on conventional energy sources is proving unsustainable. Amidst this challenge, hybrid power generation emerges as a beacon of hope. This innovative technology integrates diverse energy sources, predominantly renewables such as solar and micro-hydro, to foster a more resilient and eco-conscious electricity infrastructure. By amalgamating multiple sources, hybrid systems transcend the limitations inherent in singular-source generation. They adeptly tackle the intermittency issue of renewables like solar, which wane at night, by integrating constant sources like micro-hydro, capable of operating round the clock. This adaptability ensures a consistent and reliable power supply, crucial for Assam's burgeoning energy needs. Hybrid power generation presents a financially prudent avenue for addressing the mounting electricity requirements. By blending renewable sources with potentially lower operational expenses, these systems mitigate dependence on costly fossil fuels, thereby heralding long-term economic advantages. This paper delves into the existing hybrid power generation techniques pertinent to Assam, with a particular emphasis on the fusion of micro-hydro and solar photovoltaic (PV) cells.

articleTitle: Design, Modelling and Control of FPIM Driven Electric Vehicle based on Drive Cycle
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment (ICEPE)
abstract: The drive train design, modelling, and control of an electric vehicle powered by a five-phase induction motor (FPIM) using drive cycle based data are presented in this study. For an Electric Vehicle (EV) to operate more smoothly, safely, dependably, and without interruption, the choice of motor and control system is essential. Depending on the driving circumstances, a given motor may behave differently. An urban or suburban region’s drive cycle represents its driving pattern. Five phase induction machines have many advantages like, higher torque density, fewer torque ripples, fault tolerance, and a lower inverter switch rating. Therefore, the use FPIM as the propulsion drive is a potent solution for electric vehicles, where the main concerns of the drive selection like public safety, continuity of operation under fault, and overall high system reliability can be meet at a reasonable cost. The reference speed for the propulsion drive’s closed-loop control is produced by the urban Indian drive cycle. The three-wheel auto rickshaw’s FPIM-based propulsion drive is controlled by the rotor field-oriented control (RFOC) approach combined with the sine PWM control (SPWMC) methodology. The MATLAB/SIMULINK environment is used to model the full electric car drive system, and performance analysis of the different machine and vehicle parameters is presented.

articleTitle: VCaps-Net: Fine-Tuned VGG16 with Capsule Network for Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia Detection on a Diverse Dataset
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment (ICEPE)
abstract: Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia (ALL) is a highly malignant condition that specifically impacts White Blood Cells (WBC) derived from lymphoid cells. Given its potentially lethal nature, it is crucial to diagnose Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia (ALL) promptly. Currently, the field of medical sciences is heavily impacted by automated computer-assisted techniques that rely on Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Deep Learning (DL). These approaches are essential tools for clinicians to identify diseases rapidly and reduce their workload. This paper proposed a DL-based novel VCaps-Net framework constructed combining fined-tuned VGG16 with Capsule Network to detect ALL efficiently. The fine-tuned VGG16 features are incorporated into the capsule network to extract enhanced and highly discriminative features. Further, a diverse dataset is proposed by combining our private dataset containing 1000 smear images with a publicly accessible dataset comprising 108 images. The proposed VCaps-Net framework obtained a 98.64% accuracy rate on the diverse dataset. Furthermore, the comparative studies signify the superiority of the proposed VCaps-Net Framework over comparing methodologies.

articleTitle: A novel estimation of phase angle and amplitude errors under dynamic scenarios by Lissajous Patterns
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment (ICEPE)
abstract: The utilization of lissajous patterns in calculating absolute phase and amplitude errors under different scenarios is analysed in this paper. The scenarios include variation of phase angle and amplitude fluctuations for a sinusoidal signal with different constraints. The different constraints like addition of noise, SNR (signal to noise) variation, changing of cycles in amplitude modulated signal were considered for wider evaluation of this study. Moreover, the pearson correlation coefficient makes use of lissajous patterns which evaluates the amplitude and phase angle and then absolute errors are found out. The simulation results reveal that the proposed technique accurately estimates the absolute amplitude and phase angle error for a given sinusoidal signal under different scenarios. Thus, this work provides insight about the robustness and reliability of proposed technique in accurately characterizing sinusoidal signals under challenging conditions.

articleTitle: Design of a Novel PLL for Application in Distributed High Frequency Bands
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment (ICEPE)
abstract: This manuscript outlines the design of a high frequency distributed bands PLL which is applicable for use in various RF communication systems. The proposed PLL comprises of two voltage controlled oscillators (VCOs) operating in the range of 3.8 GHz to 7.59 GHz and 8.40 GHz to 9.54 GHz. The novelty of the PLL is along with Phase Frequency detector (PFD) and Charge Pump (CP) it utilizes different order low pass filters (LPF) depending on the frequency of operation to reduce the spur. The design is carried out in cadence 90nm GPDK. At 4.5 GHz operating frequency of the PLL, phase noises are found to be -93.15 dBc/Hz at 1Mhz and -118.79 dBc/Hz at 10 MHz whereas at 8.5 GHz the phase noises are - 89.94 dBc/Hz at 1 MHz and -115.64 at 10 MHz. The reference Spur is maintained when operating at higher frequency band due to the use of 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup> order LPF.

articleTitle: Estimation of Reliability Indices during Cyber Attacks under Generation and Peak Load Constrained Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment (ICEPE)
abstract: The SCADA system of power grid has become target for various cyber attacks due to its open standard based information and communication network. The attackers exploit the vulnerability of cyber components and intrude into local area network of control centers, substations there by modifying the critical data of system. Thus cyber attacks are playing a crucial role in impacting the power system reliability. In this paper an attack scenario of corporation LAN is chosen to alter the generation. A time to compromise model for known vulnerability is framed for altering the generation. A new type of attacks namely lion and fox attacks are introduced to showcase these attacks are prone to decrease the reliability of power system. Two standard systems are considered for evaluation of reliability under the mentioned attack scenarios with respect to generation level indices i.e. loss of load expectation (LOLE) and loss of energy expectation (LOEE). The simulation results reveal that power system becomes less reliable if the proposed generation cyber attack occurs on the system. Thus, the proposed work is suitable for the estimation of cyber threats in the future scope. Index Terms—Generation model, load model, reliability indices, cyber attacks, power system.

articleTitle: Dual Solar PV based Battery Charger for E-rickshaw Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment (ICEPE)
abstract: Solar charger for E-rickshaw is one of application whose popularity is on the rise. However, most of the solutions uses a single solar panel on top of the e-rickshaw/toto leading less utilization of space available. A dual PV based scheme is reported in literature for E-rickshaw application, but it requires higher number of semiconductor and passive components. To address the aforesaid concerns, a dual PV fed boost converter based battery charger scheme is proposed in this paper. This architecture facilitates simultaneous charging of battery from both PVs and also designed to seamlessly operate in single PV mode, ensuring uninterrupted battery charging even in scenario when one PV is damaged or removed temporarily. Additionally, over voltage protection that safeguards the battery against potential damage due to excessive charging is also included in the control algorithm. This scheme is also empowered to supply power from two PV panels of different ratings installed at different portions on the E-rickshaw. Entire converter circuit and scheme are simulated in the MATLAB/Simulink environment and results are validated for different operating modes as well as for different irradiation levels.

articleTitle: Smart Vending Machines: Improving Service Quality with Integrated Controllers and SVM Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment (ICEPE)
abstract: The retail industry is transforming with the emergence of the Internet of Things (IoT) and embedded controllers with Support Vector Machines (SVM) algorithm. This research explores the advancements in vending machines, which combine technology and embedded controllers with traditional vending machines. These intelligent devices can collect data, analyze it, and make real-time decisions thanks to their sensors, touch screens, and sophisticated embedded controllers. Through this innovation, smart vending machines can offer consumers a shopping experience based on their purchases and interactions with the machine. With data analysis capabilities, these integrated controllers enable the machines to provide discounts, special offers, and even recommendations on what to buy. In addition, intelligent vending machines help streamline inventory management, preventing shortages of popular goods. Because of this, embedded controllers are transforming vending machine operations' future while radically altering the retail industry. By collecting and analyzing data in real-time, smart vending machines allow for data-driven decision-making, which improves inventory management and reduces waste. Since all payment methods are linked flawlessly, purchasers can be sure that their transactions will go through without a problem.
