articleTitle: Isolation Forests Integration for Proactive Anomaly Detection in Augmented Reality-enhanced Tele-ICU Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment (ICEPE)
abstract: To improve patient monitoring and identify aberrant occurrences quickly, use isolation forests in augmented reality (AR)-enhanced tele-intensive care unit (Tele-ICU) systems for proactive anomaly detection. Here, we present a system that uses the ensemble machine learning technique of isolation forests to spot anomalies in the complicated and ever-changing data streams in tele-ICU settings. Our solution finds abnormalities in AR-enhanced data better than standard approaches because it uses isolation trees, which separate anomalies more rapidly. This improves healthcare quality and patient safety. The system can adjust to changing patient circumstances by incorporating isolation forests, which solve problems caused by high-dimensional and various AR-enhanced tele-ICU data. It can quickly discover anomalies and respond proactively to health problems by building isolation trees using randomly picked information. Integrating isolation forests is in sync with the real-time requirements of tele-ICU systems, enabling the rapid detection and prevention of abnormalities before worsening. By offering a practical and efficient method for detecting anomalies, the proposed framework shows potential for improving the overall performance of tele-ICU systems. To ensure the smooth functioning and safety of AR-enhanced tele-ICU settings, which contribute to better patient outcomes and healthcare delivery, healthcare organizations are increasingly embracing technological innovations. One essential tool in this integration is isolation forests.

articleTitle: Optimal Dietary Management via Data Analytics, ANN Based Health Insights, and Ecosystem for Continuous Nutrient Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment (ICEPE)
abstract: This research paper offers a groundbreaking study on precision nutrition, an intelligent Internet of Things ecosystem that aims to transform the control of nutritional intake. The system provides continuous nutritional analysis and individualized health insights due to its integration of cutting-edge sensor technology with data analytics. Real-time monitoring of the food and drinks' nutritional content is made possible by the ecosystem thanks to a network of intelligent wearable devices equipped with spectroscopic and ion-selective sensors. The technology delivers tailored health insights and dietary recommendations by using algorithms for machine learning and an extensive library of nutrients. In this article, the architecture, sensor integration, data processing, and validation procedures of the Internet of Things ecosystem are further detailed. The suggested system is accurate and effective, as shown by the results of extensive validation studies. The findings of this study highlight the potentially game-changing role that the Internet of Things (IoT) ecosystem may play in enabling people to improve their health via educated dietary decisions, contribute to the development of precision nutrition research, and maximize their health results.

articleTitle: Optimizing Combustion Efficiency in Cloud-Connected Smart Gasoline Engines using Gradient Boosting Machines
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment (ICEPE)
abstract: This research proposes using cloud-connected technologies and Gradient Boosting Machines (GBM) to improve smart Gasoline combustion efficiency. It uses real-time cloud data feeds to inform GBM decision-making to optimize fuel utilization and reduce emissions. A prediction model that adjusts to dynamic engine conditions was created using previous data and constant sensor inputs. It uses ensemble learning to optimize combustion parameters like spark timing and air-fuel ratio using GBM, improving engine performance. The experimental setup uses a cloud-connected smart petrol engine prototype with enhanced sensors and actuators. The engine and centralized computing system communicate seamlessly via the cloud architecture, allowing quick data analysis and model changes. Iterative model refinement and real-time modifications allow the system to adapt to changing operating conditions and maximize combustion efficiency. Compared to standard engine management systems, thorough calculations and practical testing reveal considerable fuel efficiency and pollution reductions. The cloud-connected GBM technique handles uncertainty and unexpected operating situations well, demonstrating its promise for smart engine systems. It advances intelligent engine control systems by using cloud connection and machine learning (ML) to optimize petrol engine combustion efficiency. The discoveries may help the car sector create environmentally friendly and high-performance engine solutions.

articleTitle: IntruderWatch: AI-Powered Computer Vision for Dynamic Intrusion Surveillance and Threat Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment (ICEPE)
abstract: IntruderWatch is an innovative smart closed-circuit television (CCTV) system engineered to revolutionize intrusion detection through the application of cutting-edge computer vision techniques. As security concerns continue to escalate in both residential and commercial domains, the imperative for advanced surveillance solutions has become increasingly pronounced. IntruderWatch represents a significant advancement in this realm, harnessing the power of sophisticated algorithms to analyze live video feeds in real-time, thereby enabling the swift and accurate identification of unauthorized individuals or activities within monitored premises. This research paper presents a comprehensive exploration of IntruderWatch, detailing its architectural design, core functionalities, and performance evaluations. Leveraging a multi-module approach, the system integrates various computer vision algorithms tailored specifically for different aspects of intrusion detection. The motion detection module employs robust algorithms to detect and track movement within the surveillance area, while the noise detection module utilizes advanced techniques to identify anomalous sounds indicative of potential threats. The identification module enhances security by implementing state-of-the-art face recognition algorithms, enabling the system to recognize known individuals and flag unknown ones for further scrutiny. Through rigorous experimentation and evaluation, the efficacy of IntruderWatch is demonstrated across diverse security scenarios, highlighting its accuracy, reliability, and scalability. The paper also discusses potential avenues for future research and development, paving the way for further advancements in intelligent surveillance systems.

articleTitle: Mutual Inductance and Magnetic Flux in Dynamic Wireless Charging for EVs with Circular and Rectangular Coils
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment (ICEPE)
abstract: Dynamic Wireless Charging (DWC) is an innovative and trending technology poised to revolutionize the electric vehicle (EV) industry. By enabling EV batteries to charge automatically while the vehicles are in motion, DWC addresses one of the major hurdles in EV adoption: range anxiety. Traditional internal combustion engine (ICE) vehicles, which have dominated the transportation sector for over a century, significantly contribute to environmental pollution through the emission of greenhouse gases and other harmful pollutants, leading to increased air pollution, global warming, and adverse health effects. In contrast, EVs, especially those utilizing DWC, offer a cleaner and more sustainable alternative, promoting the transition away from fossil fuels and supporting the broader goals of reducing carbon footprints and mitigating climate change. This paper focuses on the design of the transmitter and receiver coils used in DWC systems, specifically examining circular and rectangular coil geometries. It discusses how the mutual inductance and magnetic flux between these coils affect the efficiency and effectiveness of power transfer. By optimizing coil design and understanding the impact of mutual inductance and magnetic flux, this research aims to improve the performance of DWC technology, enhancing its convenience, appeal, and adoption, thereby contributing to a cleaner, more efficient, and environmentally friendly transportation future.

articleTitle: Predictive Analytics for Hospital Readmissions Using Logistic Regression and IoT Sensor Data
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment (ICEPE)
abstract: Hospital readmissions affect healthcare systems globally, increasing costs and morbidity. Readmissions must be predicted and prevented to improve patient outcomes and save healthcare costs. This research leverages the Internet of Things (IoT) sensor data and Logistic Regression (LR) to reduce hospital readmissions using predictive analytics. Patient health data from IoT devices during and after hospitalization is used in the paper. Heart rate, blood pressure, and oxygen saturation are constantly monitored. LR is used to examine this dataset and create a prediction model. The LR algorithm trains us to recognize IoT sensor data patterns and correlations that indicate readmission risks. Our methodology provides developed risk estimates incorporating patient-specific parameters, including age, multiple illnesses, and medical history. The temporal data permits dynamic predictions, considering patient health changes over time. This research detected hospital readmission risk with promising accuracy. These predictions allow healthcare practitioners to proactively intervene and deliver targeted treatments, including prescription modifications, lifestyle advice, and follow-up consultations to decrease readmission. This proactive strategy may improve patient outcomes and save healthcare expenses.

articleTitle: Development of Eight-legged Spider Robot Using Theo Jansen Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment (ICEPE)
abstract: In hazardous or critical situations, society needs stable robotic solutions. Traditional models frequently struggle because of their limited mobility and stability, which could hinder quick and effective interventions. Distinctive designs are required to improve performance and safety to overcome these environmental barriers. This research presents the design and development of an eight-legged spider robot that performs motion based on the Theo Jansen (TJ) mechanism. TJ’s mechanism is a user-friendly and efficient approach for locomotion, which is applied to create adaptable robots for uneven terrain. The study examines the original design, body structure, engine selection, design challenges, control system choices, and manufacturing techniques. Development and design parameters of an eight-legged robot optimized for smooth locomotion are critical. The efficacy of these robots is scrutinized, highlighting the transformative potential of Jansen’s mechanisms in advancing mobility solutions. Future research explores the broader implications of using such robots.

articleTitle: Smart Water Taps Using IoT Sensors and Deep Reinforcement Learning for Personalized Consumption Control
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment (ICEPE)
abstract: This research introduces an innovative approach to water conservation and personalized consumption management by combining Internet of Things (IoT) sensors with Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) methods. The suggested approach aims to give people more control over their water use in response to water shortages and the need for sustainable resource management. It installs IoT sensors on taps to track water use in real time. A DRL framework is fed data that these sensors have collected. The DRL algorithm develops individual consumption profiles for each user by factoring in past water use, environmental conditions, and personal tastes. Using this unique profile, water efficiency may be improved instantly. Users may easily enter their water conservation choices, budgets, and the system's user interface. Adjusting the water's flow rate by the user profiles learned by the DRL actively regulates water use while keeping people happy. The results of the experiments reveal that our method effectively reduces both water use and waste. Integrating IoT sensors with DRL methods provides a flexible and scalable answer for smart water management that economically benefits the environment and consumers.

articleTitle: IoT-based Online Condition Monitoring of Power Transformer
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment (ICEPE)
abstract: Conventional power system monitoring techniques mostly rely on human observation, which is error-prone and requires ongoing supervision. However, the successful transformation of a traditional grid to a smart grid requires smarter monitoring and control. A crucial component like transformer needs continuous monitoring to increase its efficiency and reliability thereby reducing its loss and downtime. The development of IoT (Internet of Things) technology provides a revolutionary way to improve monitoring practices. The preventive analytics is made easier by the incorporation of IoT, allowing early detection of any problems and prompt resolution to avoid downtime. This study attempts to develop an advanced online condition monitoring system for power transformers in an open-source cloud-based IoT platform, ThingSpeak. A prototype is developed in the lab using Wi-Fi integrated Node MCU microcontroller with a capability to keep an eye on vital indicators including voltage, current, temperature, humidity and oil level by integrating a variety of sensors. A novel technique of capacitance based oil level detector is also designed and presented in this paper, which can be a potential replacement of the mercury based Buchholz relay. The real-time data visualization and analysis capabilities are shown by using ThingSpeak platform as well as a customized MIT App developed for easier access to real-time data in mobile phone or any other handheld device. Additional feature of SMS notifications via IFTTT (If This Then That) is integrated in the proposed model to alarm and trigger action at the time of anomalies.

articleTitle: Development of a low-cost Gesture Controlled 3-axis Robotic System
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment (ICEPE)
abstract: This paper explores the challenge of creating a reliable gesture-controlled robotic system capable of precise movement in a fixed environment. Gesture control, while intuitive, can be sensitive and prone to malfunctions with minor disruptions. The study focuses on designing a sturdy mechanical framework to minimize interference and ensure accuracy. Testing, including simulations and real-life scenarios, validates the system’s reliability. The research outlines clear objectives to implement gesture control technology and implement it on hardware structures. By integrating basic sensing systems, image processing, actuators, and communication tools like ROS2, the aim is to simplify calibration processes for user-friendly operation. This study aims to contribute practical solutions to robotics by integrating simple yet effective technologies for precise motion control.

articleTitle: Double Auction Strategies for Peer-to-Peer Energy Trading in Smart Grids: A Game Theoretic and Blockchain Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment (ICEPE)
abstract: The concept of using blockchain technology for peer-to-peer energy trading (P2PET) in smart grids, particularly employing a double auction-based game theoretic method, is a fascinating application of both blockchain and economic principles. This paper deals with a blockchain-enabled framework for P2PET in a smart grid by using a double auction-based game theory approach. The proposed permissioned blockchain network was developed using Hyperledger Fabric, Minifab and designed by configuring the spec.yaml file. Three smart contracts, or Chaincode namely Double Auction Order, CreateP2PEnergy, and Matching, have been written using Golang and deployed into the blockchain network, thereby creating automatic energy trading transactions between energy producers and consumers. The client communication, such as consumer queries, user input, and producer trading concepts, was designed using the Postman API. Additionally, the double auction framework’s performance has been measured by Hyperledger Caliper. Analysis shows that when 1000 transactions were initiated in each round by clients using Hyperledger Caliper and REST API services, the Proof of Elapsed Time (PoET) mechanism successfully processed 946 transactions, in contrast to the 627 transactions managed by Proof of Work (PoW). The outcomes from multiple rounds of testing underscore the enhanced performance of this framework. In summary, the combination of blockchain technology, P2P energy trading, smart grids, and game theory offers a promising approach to revolutionizing the energy sector. By decentralizing energy trading, empowering consumers, and leveraging market mechanisms, this approach has the potential to enhance efficiency, promote renewable energy adoption, and foster a more sustainable energy ecosystem.

articleTitle: Power Quality Analysis of Grid-To-Vehicle & Vehicle-To-Grid Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment (ICEPE)
abstract: Power quality analysis is crucial in Grid-to- Vehicle (G2V) and Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) technologies, ensuring grid stability, reliable power flow, and equipment health. It enhances system efficiency, communication, and battery health in electric vehicles (EVs). It also ensures compliance with power quality standards, and customer satisfaction, and facilitates the integration of renewable energy. There are some common controllers used for quality improvement or harmonic reduction, such as the PI controller, LC filter, etc. This work proposes a model predictive controller for enhancement of the power quality with Electric vehicle application. The investigation of the proposed model has been developed in MATLAB Simulink and successfully tested the results.

articleTitle: Sustainable Energy Evolution Using IoT-Enhanced Carbon Capture and Storage for Oil Recovery
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment (ICEPE)
abstract: The global energy environment is shifting toward sustainability and carbon neutrality. Internet of Things (IoT) technology with Carbon Capture and Storage (CCS) in Enhanced Oil Recovery (EOR) may reduce carbon emissions and optimize hydrocarbon recovery. This paper examines IoT-enabled CCS for EOR and carbon-neutral oil and gas operations. Real-time data capture and analysis using IoT technologies optimize CCS operations. Installing IoT sensors and devices across the EOR and CCS infrastructure lets operators monitor CO2 injection rates, reservoir pressure, temperature, and fluid composition. The CCS process is precisely controlled using data, improving carbon capture efficiency and lowering operating costs. Remote monitoring and management of carbon storage sites using IoT in CCS for EOR improves environmental sustainability. The collected CO2 is securely and efficiently contained, reducing leakage and environmental effects. Preventing CCS infrastructure problems with IoT-driven predictive maintenance ensures long-term operational dependability. Securely storing collected CO2 offsets oil and gas emissions and contributes to carbon neutrality. EOR process optimization with IoT technologies may boost hydrocarbon recovery, making the switch to greener energy sources easier. IoT-enabled CCS for EOR has the potential to produce carbon-neutral oil and gas operations. The system improves CCS efficiency and sustainability using real-time data, remote monitoring, and predictive maintenance. Integration of IoT with CCS reduces carbon emissions and promotes the industry's worldwide sustainability objectives.

articleTitle: Exploring Molecular Mechanisms Through Graph Convolutional Neural Network for Protein Profiling
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment (ICEPE)
abstract: Using Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs) for extensive protein profiling, this research aims to unravel the molecular subtleties of COVID-19. The main objective is to decipher the intricate relationship between viral and human host proteins to have a better grasp of disease path physiology and possible treatment options. The goal of this study is to use GCNs to identify structural motifs, functional pathways, and critical protein-protein interactions that are involved in viral infection and the control of the host immune response. The study’s overarching goal is to aid in the creation of better diagnostic instruments, therapeutic approaches, and vaccinations against COVID-19 by clarifying these molecular pathways. By using multi-omics data, this study aims to improve GCNs' predictive power in defining new protein interactions and finding druggable targets. This study aims to speed up the identification of much-needed antiviral medicines by using cutting-edge computational approaches to shed light on the path physiology of COVID-19. The long-term objective is to address the continuing worldwide health catastrophe caused by the COVID-19 pandemic by creating a collaborative platform for multidisciplinary research that brings together computational biologists and experimental virologists. Using a variety of criteria, the Kaggle database shows (i) how two cities lived during COVID-19. (i) Bike_ID, Rental_ID, Duration in hours (min 60, max 1380), Start Station ID, which can be anything from one day to three or four days in the future, with a unique range of values from 0.0927542 to -0.197574, Latitude from 51.506 to 51.4996, and (iii) Transactions done during COVID-19 with a range of values from 1494460 to 232629023, with a class type of 1,2, or unknown, and a duration in hours (min 60, max 1380).

articleTitle: Precision Lunar Landscape Unveiled with Terrain Mapping and Advanced Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment (ICEPE)
abstract: The study introduces an innovative lunar exploration method employing deep neural networks, specifically Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), to enhance Terrain Mapping Camera (TMC) data resolution to an unprecedented 5-meter precision. The primary objective is to surpass the capabilities of the Orthogonal High-Resolution Camera (OHRC). The proposed approach will undergo rigorous validation through k-fold cross-validation, aiming to provide unparalleled insights into lunar terrain. Leveraging the refined data, the study aims to create an advanced hazard map, promising a revolutionary impact on mission planning and ensuring safer lunar navigation. Going beyond, the methodology extends to real-time navigation techniques using the enhanced TMC dataset. By integrating high-resolution techniques, hazard mapping, real-time navigation, and robust model validation, this approach has the potential to establish a new benchmark for lunar missions. The anticipated outcomes may significantly advance our understanding of lunar landscapes, enhancing safety protocols and navigation strategies for future lunar exploration endeavors.

articleTitle: Optimal Parameter Extraction and Performance Evaluation of Equivalent Circuit Models for Lithium-ion batteries under Dynamic Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment (ICEPE)
abstract: This paper thoroughly investigates lithium-ion battery (LIB) modeling via equivalent circuit models (ECMs). It evaluates ECM performance, highlighting strengths and limitations. Tests show fixed parameter models perform adequately under stable conditions, but less accurately with temperature changes. Advanced models, like the 2RC model, excel in replicating transient behavior. The study also explores ECM optimization using algorithms, with the Water Cycle Algorithm showing promising capability. Additionally, a dynamic driving schedule is used to compare and validate the accuracy of the results. The research offers valuable insights into LIB modeling, identifying future directions for temperature and state-of-charge (SOC) dependent models and ECM integration with advanced battery management algorithms.

articleTitle: Review and Analysis of WSN with Cluster Routing Issues and Provide Solutions Through Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment (ICEPE)
abstract: Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) technology has emerged extensively. Network clustering is the procedure to enhance energy efficiency. The conventional approaches resolve several issues. However, they may not develop a precise result for forecasting system behavior. In this article, we investigate WSN with Cluster routing issues and provide solutions through Artificial intelligence and Machine learning algorithms. This article describes WSN routing issues and functional issues. Also, it explains Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning (ML) techniques to solve the data collection, aggregation, and distribution issues in WSN. The significant objective of cluster formation, Cluster Head (CH) selection, and distribution algorithms is to collect and forward the data in an energy-resourceful method, as a result improving the lifetime. The benefits of clustering in WSNs comprise better scalability, minimizing delay, and raising energy efficiency. This Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning techniques applied in WSNs will be a lead for the research society in describing the typically adapted approaches for solving the issues interrelated to cluster with WSN routing.

articleTitle: Co-optimization of Reserves in Energy Market to mitigate Congestion
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment (ICEPE)
abstract: Reserves are extremely important in any competitive electricity market while eliminating congestion, to ensure the security and dependability for an optimal power system operation. Delivery times, transmission constraints, local area requirements, and the efficient utilization of energy and reserve capacity in an emergency state during outage are all factors that must be considered while procuring ancillary services to fulfill the demand. A technique of procurement of reserve services which guarantees the reliability of the system for any contingency event has been revealed in this paper through a 4-bus system where the price of ancillary services on a zonal basis explicitly depict the imports of reserves in a parallel energy market condition.

articleTitle: Decentralized Energy Using IoT and Cloud Computing for Enhancing Grid Resilience Through Microgrid Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment (ICEPE)
abstract: Climate change, cyberattacks, and renewable energy integration threaten the contemporary electrical system. This paper proposes integrating decentralized energy production, the Internet of Things (IoT), microgrids, and cloud computing to improve grid resilience. Solar panels, wind turbines, and small power plants can reduce the grid's need for centralized electricity. Microgrids may function independently or alongside the main grid during outages or crises. The IoT allows real-time energy asset and grid infrastructure monitoring, control, and optimization. IoT sensors, smart meters, and actuators gather and analyze data for proactive maintenance, problem detection, and load control. Cloud computing powers this resilient grid ecosystem with scalable, cost-effective data storage, processing, and analytics. Cloud solutions enable predictive maintenance, demand response, and grid optimization by processing massive volumes of IoT data. Using decentralized energy production, IoT, and cloud computing, grid operators may improve resilience. First, they identify and react to grid abnormalities in real time, limiting downtime and cascading failures. Second, they may optimize energy output and reduce carbon emissions by integrating renewable energy sources better. Third, sophisticated cybersecurity and predictive threat analysis may improve grid security.

articleTitle: Leveraging IoT for Real-Time Air Quality Sensing and Optimization in Vehicle Interiors using Gradient Boosting Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment (ICEPE)
abstract: The poor air quality in many contemporary metropolitan locations negatively influences people’s health, especially while users travel in their automobiles for work or school. This study suggests a novel system based on the Internet of Things (IoT) and Gradient Boosting algorithm (GD) that can monitor and regulate the air quality inside the interiors of vehicles in real-time. The system provides passengers and drivers access to vital information to create a cabin atmosphere that is more conducive to good health. This is accomplished by integrating cutting-edge sensors, data analytics, and user interfaces. The suggested solution has as its goal the provision of continuous measurements of pollutants such as particulate matter, volatile organic compounds, and carbon dioxide, in addition to the provision of actionable insights in the form of individualized suggestions and alarms. Utilizing GPS data, the system can also provide route options depending on the current air quality conditions. This study builds a bridge between the fields of environmental health and transportation technology. As a result, it contributes to improved passenger well-being, increased urban mobility, and a complete knowledge of air quality trends.

articleTitle: Techno-Economic Investigation of PV based Water Pump
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment (ICEPE)
abstract: This paper discusses practice of solar energy as a solution to significant issues we face daily. One of these issues is the availability of clean water for home usage. In these works, various strategies for an efficient water pumping system in water-scarce places are suggested. Earlier Researchers have shown how solar power can be used in place of fossil fuels by employing solar and wind energy instead. A battery charge controller (BCC) with PID, PI, or a relay and MOSFET-based controller has been employed by some researchers. For maximal power output, some engineers have solely employed buck-boost, boost, or inverter converters. For water pumping, some people have employed induction (IM) or brushless DC (BLDC) motors. All versions range in price depending on their characteristics. Due to the rising demand for water in remote areas with few water reservoirs and inadequate power supply, an efficient, nonpolluting, and cost-effective water supply model is necessary. As a result, we put out an idea for using renewable energy to pump water. The model uses solar energy to pump water using photovoltaic (PV) panels. Fuzzy logic (FL) maximum power point tracking (MPPT) is used to deliver greatest power production regardless of irradiance and temperature conditions. The FL controls battery charging & discharging to the available PV voltage. The single-stage inverter's AC output powers the BLDC motor that drives the water pump. As a result, the whole model is dependable, consumes less energy, and lasts longer. The proposed model is recommended for rural areas where water crisis is a major problem.

articleTitle: Correlating Remote Sensing Data Frequencies: Analyzing Patterns and Relationships for Predicting Solar Energy Generation
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment (ICEPE)
abstract: This research aims to explore the correlation between remote sensing data frequencies and solar energy generation for accurate prediction. By analyzing patterns and relationships, the study seeks to identify how specific frequencies in remote sensing data can be leveraged to forecast solar energy generation with heightened accuracy. In today’s renewable energy landscape, precise solar energy generation predictions are vital for efficient energy planning and grid management. The research proposes the use of remote sensing data frequencies to refine predictive models, minimizing variability and uncertainties associated with solar power production. By developing a robust framework that integrates advanced data analysis and remote sensing technologies, this study aims to empower stakeholders in optimizing resource allocation and managing solar infrastructure effectively. Ultimately, this approach will contribute to more reliable and sustainable energy systems.

articleTitle: Intelligent Integrated Vehicle Control and Motor Control Unit for Electric Three wheelers
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment (ICEPE)
abstract: Automotive industries are currently transitioning to electric vehicles, and electric three-wheelers (e3W) have become popular for urban public transportation and last-mile connectivity in India. However, many e3Ws in the country use sub-components from neighboring countries that are unsuitable for Indian conditions, lacking indigenous development. Additionally, there is a lack of a supervisory controller for safety and improved overall efficiency. To address these issues, this paper introduces the design and development of an integrated Vehicle Control Unit (VCU) cum Motor Control Unit (MCU) for low-speed electric vehicles, including e3W. The integrated controller, implemented with a single-chip dual-core microcontroller, assigns VCU functions to the master core and MCU functionality to the slave core. The VCU performs tasks such as torque re-structuring/de-rating, energy optimization, temperature monitoring, range estimation, and component safety enhancement. It interacts with signal conditioning interfaces for the motor, controller, and battery, communicating with a smart display unit to show range, fault status, distance covered, speed, etc. Meanwhile, the MCU is designed for 4quadrant drive operation with regenerative braking capabilities. The overall solution is compact, cost-effective, reliable, and scalable for various ratings, offering essential features for low-speed electric vehicles like e-rickshaws, e-autos, electric two-wheelers, etc. Experimental results from laboratory test benches and on-road testing of an actual e3W demonstrate the salient features and advantages of this technology.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Solar Irradiation Prediction using Machine Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Environment (ICEPE)
abstract: The growing energy demand has led to a greater integration of alternative energy sources, especially photovoltaic (PV) energy. For a consistent and reliable power supply, however, precise solar irradiation forecasting is essential. This problem was addressed by using machine learning methods like the k-nearest neighbor algorithm (KNN) and linear regression (LR) to provide forecasts. The historical information included in this study’s model was collected over 24 years (1998–2022). The effectiveness and uncertainties of the models are assessed through experimental evaluations that concentrate on forecast precision, correlation coefficient, and metrics like mean absolute error (MAE), root mean square error (RMSE), mean prediction interval (MPI), and prediction interval coverage probability (PICP). The study compares the models to improve solar radiation forecasting accuracy, preserve power system stability and dependability, and manage energy supply and demand.
